verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators with Alabama marketplace sales in excess of $250,000 are required to collect tax on sales made by or on behalf of their third-party sellers.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. References Alabama Department of Revenue Simplified Sellers Use Tax (SSUT); Act 2018-539. | Threshold detail: Included: Total retail sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state, sales made through a non-collecting marketplace, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator, exempt wholesale sales, exempt services. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Evaluation period: Previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: The collection obligation applies to marketplace facilitators with $100,000 or more in statewide gross sales of property, products, or services delivered into the state of Alaska in the current or previous calendar year. The collection requirement for marketplace facilitators is not in effect statewide.
notes: Enforcement date varies by jurisdiction. No statewide sales tax; over 100 local governments levy local sales taxes. Collection requirement is not statewide. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Statewide gross sales of goods, property, or products delivered into the state, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator, exempt sales. Excluded: None. Effective date: Varies by district. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2025.

verbatim_quote: A business that has nexus with Arizona, operates an online marketplace, and makes online sales on behalf of third-party merchants is required to collect and remit Arizona transaction privilege tax on all sales made through the marketplace if its gross retail proceeds or income exceed $100,000 annually.
notes: Originally effective September 20, 2016; updated effective October 1, 2019. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 2757. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross proceeds of sales of tangible personal property or services, gross income derived from business in the state, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator, rentals of personal property. Effective date: October 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $200,000 in sales only as of January 1, 2019; $150,000 in sales only as of January 1, 2020; $100,000 in sales only as of January 1, 2021.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that sells or facilitates more than $100,000 in sales or at least 200 transactions of tangible personal property, taxable services, a digital code, or specified digital products for delivery into Arkansas in the previous or current calendar year must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales made through the marketplace for delivery into Arkansas.
notes: Threshold is $100,000 OR 200 transactions. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References SB 576. | Threshold detail: Included: Aggregated sales of taxable tangible personal property or services, taxable services, digital codes, specified digital products subject to Arkansas sales or use tax delivered into a state. Excluded: Exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: July 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: The collection requirement applies to in-state marketplaces and out-of-state marketplaces with sales of tangible personal property in California that exceed $500,000 in the current or preceding calendar year.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References AB 147 and SB 92. | Threshold detail: Included: Total combined sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state by the retailer and all persons related to the retailer, nontaxable sales (e.g., sales for resale), sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Services (taxable and exempt). Effective date: April 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator with a physical presence in Colorado or economic nexus with the state must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales to Colorado consumers made through the marketplace.
notes: No specific revenue threshold stated in this source for marketplace facilitator law; applies to those with physical presence or economic nexus. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. References HB 10-1193. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators that facilitated retail sales of at least $250,000 during the prior 12-month period are required to collect and remit sales tax on behalf of their marketplace sellers.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. References Public Act No. 18-152. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross receipts from tangible personal property (including digital products and SaaS) sold into the state, exempt sales, taxable services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Sales for resale, exempt services. Effective date: July 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Threshold applies to all transactions within the 12-month period ending on September 30 immediately preceding the monthly or quarterly period when liability is established. Previous threshold rules: $250,000 and 200 transactions prior to June 30, 2019; prior rules included gross receipts from tangible personal property sold into the state and exempt sales in sales threshold only; sales for resale excluded in transactions threshold only; exempt services, taxable services, digital products and SaaS excluded. Note: thresholds are conjunctive (AND), not disjunctive (OR).

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators that have a physical presence in Florida or facilitated retail sales of at least $100,000 during the previous calendar year are required to collect and remit sales tax on behalf of their marketplace sellers.
notes: Excludes persons who solely provide travel agency services and, with certain exceptions, delivery network companies. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References Florida SB 50. | Threshold detail: Included: Taxable sales of tangible personal property delivered physically into the state. Excluded: Exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: July 1, 2021. Evaluation period: Previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that makes or facilitates taxable retail sales of $100,000 or more in aggregate in the previous or current calendar year is the retailer for each taxable retail sale it facilitates in Georgia on behalf of a marketplace seller.
notes: A franchisor is not considered a marketplace facilitator with respect to any dealer that is its franchisee. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 276. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from retail sales of tangible personal property delivered electronically or physically to a location in the state for consumption, use, or storage in the state, exempt sales. Excluded: Services (taxable and exempt), exempt resales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: January 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $250,000 or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2020.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that has physical or economic nexus with Hawaii must collect and remit sales tax on all sales into the state, including those by an unlicensed seller. Marketplace sellers may be liable for Hawaii general excise tax (GET) in some situations.
notes: No specific revenue threshold stated for marketplace facilitator law in this source; applies based on physical or economic nexus. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. References SB396 SD1. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators with a physical presence in Idaho and remote marketplace facilitators with more than $100,000 in combined sales into the state must collect and remit state tax on all sales into the state, their own and those by third-party sellers. Remote marketplaces are not responsible for collecting local sales tax.
notes: Remote marketplaces not responsible for collecting local sales tax. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 259. | Threshold detail: Included: Cumulative gross receipts from sales including taxable products and taxable services delivered into the state, exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Effective date: June 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators are required to collect tax on sales made by or on behalf of their third-party sellers in Illinois if, in the preceding 12-month period, cumulative gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property to purchasers in Illinois by the marketplace facilitator and its marketplace sellers are $100,000 or more; or the marketplace facilitator and sellers cumulatively enter into 200 or more separate transactions for the sale of tangible personal property into Illinois.
notes: Threshold is $100,000 OR 200 transactions. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References Public Act 101-0009 and Public Act 101-0604. | Threshold detail: Included: Cumulative gross receipts from sales, exempt sales. Excluded: Occasional sales, sales for resale, services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: October 1, 2018 (for state use tax); January 1, 2021 (for local use tax). Evaluation period: Quarterly review based on preceding 12-month period. Previous threshold rules: Sales made through a marketplace facilitator excluded as of January 1, 2020; $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2026.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators that make or facilitate sales in Indiana and meet the economic nexus thresholds of $100,000 in sales in Indiana must collect and remit sales tax on all taxable sales made through the marketplace.
notes: Originally effective July 1, 2019; updated effective January 1, 2024. Also applies to lodging marketplaces. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 1001. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, electronically delivered products into the state, electronically delivered services into the state, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales for resale. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2024.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that meets the economic nexus threshold and makes or facilitates Iowa sales on behalf of itself or one or more marketplace sellers must collect and remit sales tax on each facilitated taxable Iowa sale.
notes: Specific revenue or transaction threshold amounts not stated in this source; references economic nexus threshold generally. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Iowa Department of Revenue is authorized but has not done so. References SF 2417. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, specified electronically delivered products, electronically delivered services into the state, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales for resale, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Effective date: January 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace providers that make or facilitate more than $100,000 in sales of taxable property or services in Kansas during the current or immediately preceding year must register, collect, and remit sales tax on each facilitated taxable sale.
notes: As of April 1, 2022, marketplace facilitators also liable for 911 fees on prepaid wireless services. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References SB 50. | Threshold detail: Included: Cumulative gross receipt from sales by the retailer to customers in Kansas, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), digital products and SaaS, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Special rule: For marketplace facilitators, threshold is based on taxable sales. Effective date: July 1, 2021. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace providers that make or facilitate retail sales of tangible personal property, digital property, or services delivered or transferred electronically in Kentucky and meet the economic nexus threshold of $100,000 in sales or 200 or more separate transactions must register, collect, and remit sales tax on each facilitated taxable sale.
notes: Threshold is $100,000 OR 200 transactions. Marketplace providers making their own sales must obtain two sales tax permits. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 354. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property delivered or transferred electronically into the commonwealth, digital property delivered or transferred electronically into the commonwealth, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: Taxable services excluded prior to January 1, 2023.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that has economic nexus with Louisiana must collect and remit sales tax on all marketplace sales for delivery into the state. Marketplace facilitators should include all sales made through the platform when calculating the economic nexus threshold (more than $100,000 in sales of tangible personal property, electronically transferred property, or taxable services in the state).
notes: Originally effective July 1, 2020; updated effective August 1, 2023. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. References Information Bulletin No. 18-006. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of products delivered into the state, electronically transferred products, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Special rule: For marketplace facilitators, threshold is based on remote retail sales. Effective date: July 1, 2020. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to August 1, 2023.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that has economic nexus with Maine must collect and remit sales tax on all marketplace sales for delivery into the state. Marketplace facilitators should include all sales made through the platform when calculating the economic nexus threshold (more than $100,000 in sales of tangible personal property, electronically transferred property, or taxable services in the state).
notes: Originally effective October 1, 2019; updated effective January 1, 2022. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References L.D. 1452. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state, taxable services delivered into the state, exempt sales. Excluded: Exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: July 1, 2018. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2022.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that has an obligation to collect Maryland sales tax, sells or facilitates sales of tangible personal property into Maryland, and processes payments on behalf of sellers must collect and remit sales tax on all sales made through the marketplace for delivery into Maryland.
notes: No specific revenue threshold stated in this source for marketplace facilitator law. A waiver of the collection requirement is available under specific conditions including publicly traded communications company seller, written agreement, and seller licensing. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 1301 and Comptroller of Maryland Tax Alert 09-19. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace provider that makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in sales in the commonwealth in the current or prior taxable year must collect and remit tax on all taxable sales made through the marketplace in Massachusetts.
notes: Applies to both remote and non-remote marketplace facilitators exceeding $100,000 threshold. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References H. 4000. | Threshold detail: Included: Sales of tangible personal property delivered into the commonwealth, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the commonwealth, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: October 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: Economic nexus is established when, in the previous calendar year, a remote marketplace facilitator has more than $100,000 in gross receipts from direct and facilitated sales into Michigan, or at least 200 direct or facilitated transactions in the state.
notes: Threshold is $100,000 OR 200 transactions. Applies to both in-state and remote facilitators with economic nexus. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 4540 and HB 4542. | Threshold detail: Included: Sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Effective date: September 30, 2018. Evaluation period: Previous calendar year.

verbatim_quote: Economic nexus is established when a remote marketplace provider makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in sales or at least 200 transactions in the state during the prior 12-month period.
notes: Originally effective October 1, 2018; amended October 1, 2019. Threshold is $100,000 OR 200 transactions. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HF 1 and HF 5. | Threshold detail: Included: Retail sales made into the state from outside the state, taxable services, exempt sales, sales to tax-exempt entities, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Sales for resale, exempt services, taxable resales. Effective date: October 1, 2019. Evaluation period: Threshold applies to the prior 12-month period. Previous threshold rules: 10 or more sales totaling $100,000 or 100 transactions prior to October 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators should include all sales made through the platform when calculating the economic nexus threshold (more than $250,000 in sales of tangible personal property or taxable services in the state). The law exempts third-party food delivery and includes an election for marketplace sellers with more than $1 billion in national revenue (including sales of affiliates and franchised entities) to directly collect sales and use tax.
notes: Law exempts third-party food delivery. Marketplace sellers with more than $1 billion in national revenue may elect to directly collect sales and use tax. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References HB 379. | Threshold detail: Included: Total sales made into the state by remote sellers that purposefully or systematically exploit the market in the state, services (taxable and exempt), exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Effective date: September 1, 2018. Evaluation period: Threshold applies to all transactions for the prior 12 months.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace provider that makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in the state in the current or previous calendar year (determined quarterly) must collect and remit sales tax on behalf of its third-party sellers.
notes: Threshold determined quarterly. Does not apply to certain advertising services, travel agency services, or third-party payment processors. Marketplace sellers relieved of duty to collect but may still be required to register and report all Missouri sales. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. References SB 153. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross receipts from taxable sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state, sales of tangible personal property made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales for resale, returned sales. Effective date: January 1, 2023. Evaluation period: Preceding 12-month period, determined each calendar quarter.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace provider that makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions in the state in the current or previous calendar year must collect and remit sales tax on behalf of its third-party sellers. Although marketplace sellers are relieved of the duty to collect or remit sales tax on sales made through a collecting marketplace, they must still register with the state and report all Nebraska sales.
notes: Marketplace sellers relieved of collection duty but must still register with state and report all Nebraska sales. | Threshold detail: Included: Total retail sales made to customers in the state, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Sales for resale, sublease, or subrent. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: April 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace provider is required to collect tax on behalf of sellers in Nevada if, in the current or immediately preceding calendar year, it had cumulative gross receipts exceeding $100,000 from retail sales made or facilitated to customers in Nevada, or made or facilitated at least 200 separate retail sales transactions in the current or preceding calendar year. A marketplace and a seller can agree, in writing, to have the seller collect the tax due instead.
notes: A marketplace and seller can agree in writing to have the seller collect the tax due instead. Nevada reports non-collecting seller use tax in some cases. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from retail sales of tangible personal property into the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Sales for resale, services (taxable and exempt). Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: October 1, 2018.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator is required to collect and remit sales tax on sales made through any physical or electronic marketplace owned, operated, or controlled by a marketplace facilitator, even if the marketplace seller is registered with New Jersey for the collection and remittance of sales tax. However, a marketplace facilitator and marketplace seller may enter into an agreement with each other regarding the collection and remittance of sales tax.
notes: No revenue or transaction threshold stated in source for New Jersey. Marketplace facilitator and seller may enter into agreement regarding collection and remittance. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace provider with at least $100,000 in total taxable gross receipts from sales in the state in the previous calendar year must register with the state and remit gross receipts tax on all sales made or facilitated in the state.
notes: Tax type is gross receipts tax, not sales tax. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Total taxable gross receipts from sales, leases, and licenses of tangible personal property, sales from licenses and services for use of real property, digital products and SaaS, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Exempt sales, exempt services. Evaluation period: Previous calendar year. Effective date: July 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace provider that made or facilitated more than $500,000 in gross sales and 100 transactions in the state in the preceding four quarterly periods is required to obtain a certificate of authority, collect sales tax, file returns, and remit tax on all sales into the state. All in-state marketplaces are required to collect tax on all sales in the state.
notes: Both revenue AND transaction thresholds must be met for remote providers. All in-state marketplaces required to collect on all sales regardless of threshold. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Cumulative total gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state, SaaS (counts as tangible personal property), nontaxable retail sales of tangible personal property, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Services (taxable and exempt). Evaluation period: Immediately preceding four sales tax quarters. Effective date: June 21, 2018. Note: Both revenue AND transaction thresholds must be met (and).

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace facilitator that made or facilitated more than $100,000 in gross sales in the state in the previous or current calendar year is required to obtain a certificate of registration, collect sales tax, file returns, and remit tax on all sales into the state. A marketplace and a seller can agree, in writing, to have the seller collect the tax due instead.
notes: Updated effective July 1, 2024. Marketplace and seller can agree in writing to have seller collect tax. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross sales sourced to the state, sum total sales price of tangible personal property, sum total sales price of digital property, sum total sales price of services, exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: November 1, 2018. Previous threshold rules: Sales or transaction volume prior to July 1, 2024.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace facilitator must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales into the state if it makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in gross sales of tangible personal property or other taxable items in the state in the current or previous calendar year.
notes: Source states enforcement date as October 1, 2019; updated effective January 1, 2019 — dates appear contradictory in source; extracted as stated. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross taxable sales of tangible personal property and other items into the state, gross taxable sales of services into the state. Excluded: Exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Previous threshold rules: Sales or transactions included prior to July 1, 2019; $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace facilitator must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales into the state if it makes or facilitates more than $100,000 in gross sales or at least 200 transactions of taxable or exempt tangible personal property or services in the state in the current or previous calendar year.
notes: Threshold applies to taxable or exempt tangible personal property or services. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property for storage, use, or consumption in the state, enumerated services the benefit of which is realized in the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Sales for resale, exempt services. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: August 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: A remote seller, marketplace facilitator, or referrer with aggregate sales of at least $10,000 in Oklahoma must file an election with the Tax Commission to either collect and remit sales and use tax on behalf of remote sellers or comply with non-collecting seller use tax notice and reporting requirements. Marketplace facilitators, referrers, or remote sellers with a place of business in Oklahoma must collect tax on their own sales.
notes: Amended as of November 1, 2019. At $10,000 threshold, facilitator must elect to either collect/remit or comply with non-collecting seller use tax notice and reporting requirements. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. | Threshold detail: Included: Aggregate sales of taxable tangible personal property, taxable services. Excluded: Exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: August 1, 2019. Previous threshold rules: $10,000 in aggregate sales of taxable TPP over the preceding 12 calendar months from July 1, 2018, through October 31, 2019; taxable and exempt services excluded from threshold prior to November 1, 2023.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that maintains a place of business in the commonwealth is required to collect and remit sales tax on the taxable sales made through its forum by any marketplace seller using the forum. A marketplace facilitator that doesn't maintain a place of business in the commonwealth and makes or facilitates $10,000 or more in taxable sales to Pennsylvania customers in the previous calendar year must register to collect and remit Pennsylvania sales tax or comply with notice and reporting requirements. Effective July 1, 2019, a remote marketplace facilitator with more than $100,000 in Pennsylvania sales in the previous 12 months is required to collect and remit sales tax on all sales into the commonwealth (i.e., cannot opt out by complying with non-collecting seller use tax reporting requirements).
notes: Initial enforcement date April 1, 2018 with $10,000 threshold and opt-out option; effective July 1, 2019, remote facilitators above $100,000 cannot opt out. Revenue threshold recorded as $100,000 reflecting the binding post-July 2019 requirement. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross sales of products and services in the commonwealth, sales by agents/representatives/subsidiaries in the commonwealth, exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a marketplace facilitator that does not collect sales tax on behalf of a remote seller. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator that collects sales tax on behalf of a remote seller. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: July 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators are required to collect and remit sales tax on 'mail-order sales' of tangible personal property, specified digital products, and taxable services after December 31, 2019. In addition, they're responsible for collecting Puerto Rico sales and use tax on behalf of third-party sellers. The collection requirement for marketplace facilitators was signed into law on April 16, 2020, with an effective date retroactive to January 1, 2020. The Puerto Rico Department of Treasury has yet to issue guidance regarding marketplace facilitator obligations for sales prior to April 16, 2020.
notes: Law signed April 16, 2020, retroactive to January 1, 2020. No guidance issued for sales prior to April 16, 2020 as of source publication. No revenue or transaction threshold stated in source. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators that meet the economic nexus threshold of more than $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 or more transactions are required to collect and remit sales tax on behalf of all sellers making sales in Rhode Island through the marketplace (third-party or marketplace sellers), even those whose sales into the state are below the economic nexus threshold.
notes: Covers all sellers including those below economic nexus threshold. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, prewritten computer software delivered electronically, load and leave/vendor-hosted prewritten computer software, specified digital products, taxable services delivered into the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: Exempt services. Evaluation period: Previous calendar year. Effective date: July 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: Online marketplace facilitators without a physical presence but with more than $100,000 in gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, products transferred electronically, and services delivered into the state are required to register and collect sales and use tax on all sales made through the marketplace.
notes: Enforcement date November 1, 2018; reinforced April 26, 2019. South Carolina defines the online marketplace itself as the retailer. In-state marketplaces with physical presence must collect on all taxable sales regardless of threshold. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, electronically transferred products, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Previous or current calendar year. Effective date: November 1, 2018.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace provider must collect and remit sales tax on all sales it facilitates into South Dakota if, in the current or preceding calendar year: The marketplace provider is a remote seller with $100,000 or more in gross sales in South Dakota; The marketplace provider facilitates sales for at least one marketplace seller that exceeds that $100,000 sales; or The marketplace provider facilitates the sales of two or more marketplace sellers that, when their sales are combined, exceed the $100,000 sales threshold
notes: Threshold can be met by facilitator's own sales, a single seller's sales, or combined sales of two or more sellers. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, electronically transferred products, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Previous or current calendar year. Effective date: November 1, 2018. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2023.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator that made or facilitated more than $100,000 in total sales to customers in Tennessee during the previous 12-month period is required to collect and remit Tennessee sales tax on behalf of its third-party sellers.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Sales to customers in the state, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt). Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator, sales for resale. Evaluation period: Previous 12-month period. Effective date: July 1, 2019. Previous threshold rules: $500,000 in sales only prior to October 1, 2020; marketplace sales included prior to October 1, 2020.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace provider that has an obligation to collect Texas sales or use tax and sells or facilitates sales of taxable items into Texas must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales made through the marketplace for delivery into Texas.
notes: No specific revenue or transaction threshold stated in source for marketplace facilitator law; obligation tied to existing Texas sales/use tax collection obligation. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $500,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator must collect and remit sales or use tax on all sales into Utah if, in the previous or current calendar year, it has more than $100,000 in gross revenue in Utah or makes at least 200 separate transactions in the state. When calculating the threshold, a marketplace should include all sales made through the platform, its own and third-party sales.
notes: Threshold includes own and third-party sales. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property and services into the state, any product transferred electronically into the state, services (taxable and exempt) rendered in the state, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: January 1, 2019. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2025.

verbatim_quote: A marketplace facilitator must collect and remit the sales tax on retail sales in Vermont by marketplace sellers through the marketplace if, during any 12-month period, it facilitated sales by marketplace sellers to destinations in Vermont of at least $100,000, or totaling at least 200 individual sales transactions.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes, in some cases. | Threshold detail: Included: Sales of tangible personal property and services into the state, products transferred electronically, services (taxable and exempt) in the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Previous 12-month period. Effective date: July 1, 2018. Note: Businesses that only sell tax-exempt items into Vermont are not required to register for sales tax.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators who contract with a marketplace seller to facilitate the sale of their products in Virginia through a physical or electronic marketplace and have more than $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 or more transactions in the commonwealth must collect and remit sales and use tax on all marketplace transactions. The threshold refers to all Virginia sales made through the marketplace — its own and third-party sales.
notes: Waiver available for marketplace sellers that already have or establish economic nexus with Virginia after July 1, 2019. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Sales of tangible personal property, products transferred electronically, taxable services, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales for resale, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: July 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators with no physical presence in the state and more than $100,000 in gross retail sales in the state in the current or preceding calendar year must collect Washington retail sales tax on taxable retail sales. As of January 1, 2020, the $100,000 threshold is based on cumulative gross income in Washington, not retail sales. The threshold refers to all Washington sales made through the marketplace — its own and third-party sales.
notes: Amended March 14, 2019. As of January 1, 2020, threshold based on cumulative gross income, not retail sales. May also have B&O tax obligation. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: Yes, in some cases. | Threshold detail: Included: Cumulative gross annual income, exempt sales, services (taxable and exempt), sales for resale, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Previous threshold rules: Cumulative gross receipts from retail sales and taxable services into the state prior to December 31, 2019; cumulative gross annual income as of January 1, 2020; resales included as of January 1, 2020.

verbatim_quote: Marketplace facilitators must collect and remit sales tax on all sales into the district, both their own and those by third-party sellers.
notes: No revenue or transaction threshold stated in source. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | No explicit marketplace facilitator threshold stated. Economic nexus threshold for remote sellers is $100,000 — verify whether this applies to marketplace facilitators specifically.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace facilitator with more than $100,000 in gross revenue from West Virginia sales or 200 or more transactions in the state in the current or preceding calendar year must collect and remit sales tax on all sales made or facilitated in the state.
notes: Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Gross sales of tangible personal property and services into the state, exempt sales, exempt services, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: January 1, 2019.

verbatim_quote: A remote marketplace facilitator with more than $100,000 in gross revenue from Wisconsin sales in the state in the current or preceding calendar year must collect and remit sales tax on all sales made or facilitated in the state. A transaction threshold was eliminated effective February 20, 2021.
notes: Transaction threshold was eliminated effective February 20, 2021. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Annual gross sales of tangible personal property into the state, annual gross sales of services (taxable and exempt) into the state, exempt sales, sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Excluded: None. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: October 1, 2018. Note: Businesses that make only nontaxable sales into Wisconsin are not required to register for sales tax. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to February 20, 2021.

verbatim_quote: An in-state marketplace facilitator must collect and remit sales tax on all sales facilitated and sold into Wyoming, regardless of whether the marketplace seller has a sales tax permit or is otherwise required to collect sales tax. A remote marketplace facilitator must collect and remit Wyoming tax on all marketplace sales if it has $100,000 in gross sales in Wyoming for delivery in Wyoming during the current or preceding calendar year.
notes: Updated effective July 1, 2024. In-state facilitators must collect on all sales regardless of threshold. Remote facilitators subject to $100,000 threshold. Non-collecting seller use tax reporting: No. | Threshold detail: Included: Annual gross sales of tangible personal property into the state, annual gross sales of services (taxable and exempt) into the state, annual gross sales of admission into the state, taxable/exempt/wholesale sales, exempt sales. Excluded: Sales made through a registered marketplace facilitator. Evaluation period: Current or previous calendar year. Effective date: February 1, 2019. Previous threshold rules: $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions prior to July 1, 2024.
